 Order

This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of bail relating to Crime No. 127 of 2023 registered at Police Station Kotwali Vidisha, District Vidisha (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 363, 366, 376, 376 (2) (N), 376 (3), 323, 344 of IPC and Section 5L/6 of POCSO Act.
Learned counsel for the applicant argued that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
The entire prosecution story is highly improbable and suspicious.

Earlier also the same prosecutrix Ajay Goud vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91790050/
1 has lodged a report under Section 363 of IPC against present applicant/accused which was registered at Crime No.76 of 2022 in that case.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that in earlier case having Crime No. 76 of 2022, the age of the prosecutrix was mentioned at 16 years, however, in the present case bearing Crime No.127 of 2023 which was registered after one and half year, her age is mentioned at 15 years, therefore, the fact of prosecutrix being minor at the time of incident becomes suspicious.

Further submission is that allegedly prosecutrix got missing on 20.02.2023 and recovered on 17.09.2023 after almost seven months, however, there is no evidence that she raised alarm and tried to escape while she was taken away by the applicant/accused.
In MLC, no definite opinion of rape has been given.
The applicant/accused is under custody since 18.12.2023.
After conclusion of investigation, charge-sheet has already been filed, therefore, no custodial interrogation is not required anymore.
The applicant is the permanent resident of District Vidisha (M.P.) and there is no possibility of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
Hence, prayed for grant of bail to the applicant.

On the other hand, learned Additional Advocate General for respondent No.1/State as well as the counsel for the respondent No.2/complainant vehemently opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/Committal Court.

E- copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance, if possible, by the office of this Court.
Certified copy as per rules.
